title: How Sam Parr saves over 50% of his income: a 7-step savings system
summary: Sam Parr explains his personal finance process from his early 20s: track spending obsessively, calculate burn and runway, set tiered savings goals up to 36 months, and deliberately feel the pain of underspending. The point is financial independence, not being cheap. Written in 2019 on his old blog.

principles.text: Saving is not being cheap; it frees money for things that truly make you happy instead of empty overconsumption.
principles.quote: Saving is **not** being cheap. It’s about having money to spend on things that truly make you happy instead of over consuming on stuff that leaves you empty.

principles.text: Entrepreneurs should hold far more runway than the standard 6 months because income is the first thing to stop.
principles.quote: I’m also very conservative with money as I’m an entrepreneur. When business is booming, I’m rolling in it. But when business sucks or I’m starting something new, my income is the first thing that stops.

principles.text: Know your numbers: average trailing 3 months of spending as burn, divide liquid assets by burn to get runway.
principles.quote: Look at your trailing 3 months of spending on Personal Capital. Average it. That’s your burn. In your spreadsheet, divide that by your liquid assets. That’s your runway.

principles.text: Track every expense manually; measuring something forces you to notice it and usually improves it.
principles.quote: tracking something forces you to notice it and typically leads to improvement.

principles.text: Set stepped runway benchmarks (3, 6, 12, 24, 36 months) and reach each before aiming for the next.
principles.quote: 3 months, 6 months, 12 months, 24 months, 36 months. Make those your benchmarks. If you have less than 3 months in cash, your goal is to get there first.

principles.text: Cut what doesn't make you happy and aim for a 50% savings rate; if you're not hurting, you're not saving enough.
principles.quote: If you’re not hurting then you’re not saving enough. Just do it.
